Plot neighbourhood UMAP with optional cell-level and edge overlays

Source: R/plot_nhood_umap.R
plot_nhood_umap.Rd

Supports three composited layers:

  1. Cell-level UMAP scatter (optional)

  2. Neighbourhood-to-neighbourhood edges (optional)

  3. Neighbourhood centroids (always shown)

Usage

plot_nhood_umap(
  nhood_umap,
  nhood_col = "community_id",
  x_col = "mean_UMAP_1",
  y_col = "mean_UMAP_2",
  fill_by = NULL,
  colour = NULL,
  size_by = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  show_edges = FALSE,
  nhood_connections = NULL,
  edge_col_1 = "mc_1",
  edge_col_2 = "mc_2",
  edge_colour = "grey70",
  edge_linewidth = 0.3,
  edge_alpha = 0.6,
  show_cells = FALSE,
  cell_umap_coords = NULL,
  cell_x_col = "UMAP_1",
  cell_y_col = "UMAP_2",
  cell_colour_by = NULL,
  cell_nhood_col = "nhood_id",
  cell_colour = NULL,
  cell_size = 0.3,
  cell_alpha = 0.5
)

Arguments

nhood_umap

A dataframe of neighbourhood centroids. Must contain neighbourhood IDs, UMAP coordinates, and any column used for fill_by or size_by. Typically SCE@metadata$coords merged with SCE@metadata$merged_nhood_analysis.

nhood_col

Name of the neighbourhood ID column in nhood_umap (default "community_id").

x_col

Name of the UMAP x-coordinate column in nhood_umap (default "mean_UMAP_1").

y_col

Name of the UMAP y-coordinate column in nhood_umap (default "mean_UMAP_2").

fill_by

Name of a column in nhood_umap to colour neighbourhood centroids by (e.g. "CD8" for assigned cell type). If NULL, uses colour as a single fixed colour.

colour

Controls neighbourhood centroid colour and depends on fill_by:

  • When fill_by is NULL — a single hex colour string (default "#3f4788" when colour is left NULL).

  • When fill_by is a column name — a named character vector mapping values in fill_by to hex colour strings. Names must cover all levels present in fill_by. If left NULL, a default categorical palette is generated automatically.

size_by

Name of a numeric column in nhood_umap to map centroid point size to, or NULL (default) for a fixed point size.

size

Controls centroid point size and depends on size_by:

  • When size_by is NULL — a single numeric giving the fixed point size (default 2 when size is left NULL).

  • When size_by is a column name — a numeric vector of length 2 giving the minimum and maximum point size of the size scale (default c(1, 5) when size is left NULL).

show_edges

Logical. Whether to draw edges between connected neighbourhoods (default FALSE).

nhood_connections

A dataframe with columns listing connected neighbourhood pairs.Self-loops are silently removed. Required when show_edges = TRUE.

edge_col_1

Name of the first neighbourhood ID column in nhood_connections (default "mc_1").

edge_col_2

Name of the second neighbourhood ID column in nhood_connections (default "mc_2").

edge_colour

Colour for edges (default "grey70").

edge_linewidth

Linewidth for edges (default 0.3).

edge_alpha

Alpha for edges (default 0.6).

show_cells

Logical. Whether to draw cell-level scatter as the bottom layer (default FALSE).

cell_umap_coords

A dataframe with one row per cell containing UMAP coordinates and any cell-level metadata columns. Required when show_cells = TRUE.

cell_x_col

Name of the UMAP x-coordinate column in cell_umap_coords (default "UMAP_1").

cell_y_col

Name of the UMAP y-coordinate column in cell_umap_coords (default "UMAP_2").

cell_colour_by

Either the name of a column in cell_umap_coords to colour cells by, or the string "nhood" to inherit the neighbourhood colour via colour and cell_nhood_col. Set NULL (default) for a fixed grey cell colour.

cell_nhood_col

Name of the column in cell_umap_coords that holds each cell's neighbourhood assignment. Required when cell_colour_by = "nhood" (default "nhood_id").

cell_colour

Controls cell point colour and depends on cell_colour_by:

  • When cell_colour_by is NULL — a single hex colour string (default "grey80" when cell_colour is left NULL).

  • When cell_colour_by is "nhood" — ignored; colour is inherited from colour via each cell's neighbourhood assignment.

  • When cell_colour_by is any other column name — a named character vector mapping values of cell_colour_by to hex colour strings. If left NULL, a default categorical palette is generated automatically.

cell_size

Fixed point size for cells (default 0.3).

cell_alpha

Alpha for cell points (default 0.5).

Value

A ggplot object. Layers are composited in the order cells (optional) -> edges (optional) -> neighbourhood centroids, so the result can be extended with further ggplot2 layers, scales or themes.

Details

Layer order (bottom to top): cells → edges → neighbourhood centroids.

See also

create_communities and test_resolution for generating the neighbourhood assignments plotted here; nhood_umap and test_resolution for generating the neighbourhood umap coordinates; nhood_annotation for annotating neighbourhoods

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Neighbourhood centroids coloured by assigned cell type ---------------
plot_nhood_umap(
  nhood_umap = nhood_df,
  fill_by    = "CD8",
  colour     = celltype_colours
)

# --- Neighbourhood centroids with default palette -------------------------
plot_nhood_umap(
  nhood_umap = nhood_df,
  fill_by    = "CD8"
)

# --- Neighbourhood centroids scaled by neighbourhood size -----------------
plot_nhood_umap(
  nhood_umap = nhood_df,
  size_by    = "n_cells",
  size       = c(1, 6)
)

# --- Neighbourhood centroids, edges and cells -----------------------------
plot_nhood_umap(
  nhood_umap        = nhood_df,
  fill_by           = "CD8",
  colour            = celltype_colours,
  show_edges        = TRUE,
  nhood_connections = connections_df,
  show_cells        = TRUE,
  cell_umap_coords  = cell_df,
  cell_colour_by    = "nhood",
  cell_nhood_col    = "nhood_id"
)

# --- Neighbourhood centroids, edges and cells coloured independently ------
plot_nhood_umap(
  nhood_umap       = nhood_df,
  fill_by          = "CD8",
  colour           = celltype_colours,
  show_cells       = TRUE,
  cell_umap_coords = cell_df,
  cell_colour_by   = "timepoint",
  cell_colour      = c(Pre = "#8da0cb", On = "#fc8d62")
)
} # }
